issues.quote: (This is PostgreSQL’s READ COMMITTED; at REPEATABLE READ the waiter would get an error and retry.)
issues.problem: Three added clarifications (PauseAndThink body line 71, Fig 2·e step 3 line 87, prose line 95) explain the approach 4 mechanism only through PostgreSQL and say that at REPEATABLE READ the waiter errors and must retry. The class demo ran on MySQL at its default isolation level, REPEATABLE READ, and filled all 120 seats on every run with no errors. A reader is led to think the demo's result depended on READ COMMITTED, or would fail at the default level, which contradicts what the class saw. The PostgreSQL behaviour is correct, but MySQL's behaviour is missing.
issues.evidence: L-0065 (MySQL), L-0112 (all 120, every run), L-0115; factcheck_applied.md §3 L-0115 (A-C-11) and L-0092 (MySQL default REPEATABLE READ)
issues.fix: Add one clause each time, e.g. at line 95: "In MySQL, where the demo ran at its default REPEATABLE READ, a locking read always reads the latest committed version of the row, so the waiter re-checks and moves on exactly as in the run <Cite href="https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/innodb-locking-reads.html">dev.mysql.com</Cite>; the error at REPEATABLE READ is PostgreSQL's behaviour." In step 3 write "(In MySQL, as in the demo, this happens at the default REPEATABLE READ too; PostgreSQL at REPEATABLE READ would instead raise an error to retry.)" Same change in the PauseAndThink body at line 71.

issues.quote: The best case for the bug is simple to state. If all 120 transactions start while the first seat is still free, all 120 book that one seat.
issues.problem: When all 120 passengers get one seat, that is the worst outcome of the bug, not the best case. It is the extreme the class described.
issues.fix: "The extreme case is simple to state. If all 120 transactions start while the first seat is still free, all 120 book that one seat. [[L-0090]]"

issues.quote: More exactly, goroutines start with small stacks that grow as needed, and the Go runtime multiplexes them onto OS threads, so one blocked goroutine doesn't stall the others. That is why 120 simultaneous passengers cost almost nothing to simulate.
issues.problem: The verified addition for L-0080 (A-KSD-20) says goroutines share one address space and are multiplexed onto a few OS threads. That nuance is what qualifies the class's 'running in its own space', and the page leaves it out. The page uses its own wording instead, and its last sentence ('cost almost nothing') is unsourced.
issues.fix: "More exactly, a goroutine is a lightweight function managed by the Go runtime: many goroutines share one address space and are multiplexed onto a small number of OS threads <Cite href="https://go.dev/doc/effective_go">go.dev</Cite>." Drop the 'cost almost nothing' sentence.
